set.body:
Defect: Revision 2 shipped `enum Coded` and recorded a vet's judgement that a forgeable Known/Unmapped was harmless. A third review disproved that BY PROBE: Scala 3 enum cases are case classes, so Known(unmapped.raw) compiles from outside and fabricates a decode that never happened -- genuine coordinate, invented interpretation status. NotApplicable would likewise take an arbitrary predicate. This hole survived two review passes precisely because one of them had written a justification for it.

Do: sealed trait Coded[+A]; final class Known[+A] private[corpus] (raw: Raw[A]); final class Unmapped private[corpus] (raw: Raw[String]); final class NotApplicable private[corpus] (raw, condition: Applicability). Checked results of decoding against a profile, a code book and the applicable row context -- never publicly constructible. Applicability (WhenColumnEquals(column, code)) ships HERE, not in P3: NotApplicable references it and the minimum subset does not compile otherwise.

Tests: Probe Known/Unmapped/NotApplicable independently of Raw, from storymodel4s.consumer.

Mutants (SD1 — each must die, recorded by name): make Coded an enum again -> the consumer probe must fail. Let NotApplicable take a raw String predicate -> the typed-Applicability test must fail.

Exit: No consumer can assert that a literal decoded, or that a condition applied.

Plan: docs/plans/2026-09-17-annotation-intake-contract.md S1 'Guarantee 2'
set.title: intake P1: Coded as checked, non-case decode results (NOT an enum)
